title: Embeddings cache: prefetching, TTL strategy, and dedupe sharding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a second-generation embeddings cache focused on three capabilities: (1) safe content hashing and normalization for deduplication across tenants and requests, (2) prefix-aware caching and opportunistic prefetch to reduce tail latency for long-context reranking flows, and (3) practical invalidation/TTL policies that balance freshness when models change with cost savings. Deliverables: implementation, tests, telemetry, and a staged rollout with feature flag gating.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end cache hit reduces end-to-end embedding compute by >=20% for synthetic duplicate-heavy workloads at 10k QPS
P50 embedding latency on cached requests improves by >=15ms and P95 improves by >=30ms in reranking scenarios
No customer-visible regressions when a model is rolled; keys are versioned and invalidated automatically
Can be toggled per-tenant via feature flag and has an ops endpoint to purge key prefixes
Unit and integration tests for normalization, hash collisions, and prefetch correctness added to CI
implementation_notes: Key format: v2:{model_checksum}:{norm_hash}:{prefix_bucket}:{attrs_hash} — includes model checksum to support safe invalidation when model weights or tokenizer change
Normalization pipeline: trim -> unicode NFKC -> collapsible whitespace -> optional lowercasing (model-config driven) -> tokenization-agnostic canonical spacing
Hash function: xxHash64 for speed; collisions mitigated by including payload-length and a 16-bit checksum (murmur3) in the cache key; unit tests simulate 1B randomized inputs to verify collision rate

Prefix-aware caching: store prefix entries for repeated leading context sequences (e.g., user profile or long doc header). Prefix bucketization uses bloom-filtered prefix fingerprints to limit memory blowup

Prefetch policy: when a request misses but shares a high-probability prefix with recent requests (based on per-shard hot-list), schedule an asynchronous prefetch for the remaining suffix embeddings up to a configurable budget
Sharding and dedupe: cache is sharded by tenant_id % N in Dedicated and by consistent hashing of norm_hash in Hosted to localize hot keys and reduce cross-shard coordination
Eviction and TTL: default TTL=24h for general workloads, TTL=72h for pinned or enterprise workloads; LRU within shard; background compaction process to garbage-collect expired prefix buckets

Invalidation: model-version bump increments model_checksum namespace, effectively invalidating old keys. For manual invalidation we expose /ops/cache/purge?prefix=... and a console action for tenant admins
Staleness mitigation: for high-traffic keys older than 48h, schedule background re-embedding if model checksum unchanged but model-ops requested increased precision (controlled by release flags)
Persistence layer: Redis (Cluster mode) for hosted small objects, with optional RocksDB-backed local LRU for Dedicated pools to avoid cross-RPCs for extremely hot keys
Backwards compatibility: existing v1 cache remains readable for 30 days; fallback logic prefers v2 when the feature flag is enabled

Telemetry: new metrics per cache-shard: cache_hits, cache_misses, prefetch_attempts, prefetch_successes, collision_count, avg_lookup_latency_ms. Add alert when collision_count ratio > 0.0001 or prefetch_success_rate < 40%
tradeoffs_and_open_questions: Normalized canonicalization reduces duplication but risks losing model-sensitive casing signals for certain tokenizers — proposed config to toggle lowercasing per model
Aggressive prefix prefetch reduces tail latency but increases upstream egress/cost if prefetch budget poorly tuned — initial budget set to 0.5% of traffic and can be increased via staged canary
Using xxHash64 favors speed over cryptographic guarantees; for tenants with high-security requirements we can add HMAC with tenant key but that increases CPU cost
Choice of TTL: 24h as conservative default to capture typical semantic stability vs cost. Some customers (news/finance) may require shorter TTLs; expose per-tenant overrides
Eviction policy complexity: LRU is simple but may thrash with prefix buckets; considering segmented LRU (SLRU) in a follow-up if we see thrashing
rollout_plan: Canary: enable for 5% of hosted traffic and 2 Dedicated customers for 48h, monitor cache hit rate and tail latency metrics
Ramp: 25% -> 60% -> 100% over two weeks if gating metrics (cache hit delta, prefetch success rate, collision_count) are healthy
Dedicated: provide migration guide and a one-click console option to enable; recommend initial TTL 72h for enterprise tenants
Kill switch: global disable via configuration and per-shard emergency purge endpoint
test_and_load_plan: Unit tests for normalization boundary cases, hash collisions, and key format parsing
Integration tests: end-to-end embedding request path with cache enabled/disabled, verifying telemetry emitted
Fuzz tests: random unicode inputs to validate normalization and collision rates
Load tests: synthetic duplicate-heavy workload at 10k QPS and mix of 30% duplicate, 50% near-duplicate (prefix-shared) to validate hit/miss and prefetch cost
Chaos tests: shard failure/redis node failure to verify fallback to compute and no request loss
